name: MonarchDashboardGrid
title: DashboardGrid
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Fixed and GridItemSpan, sized from androidx.compose.foundation.layout.BoxWithConstraints; MonarchSortableGrid in edit mode
summary: The responsive grid a dashboard's widgets sit in: one column on phones, more on wide screens, widgets spanning columns, and an edit mode in which people rearrange widgets by dragging or with buttons.
whenToUse: For a dashboard screen of MonarchWidget cards whose order each person may arrange and save.
whenNotToUse: For tiles of equal weight that are always reorderable use MonarchSortableGrid. For a fixed layout of a few cards use a Column or a Material 3 adaptive layout. For a list use LazyColumn.
api: @Composable public fun <T> MonarchDashboardGrid(items: List<T>, key: (T) -> String, itemLabel: (T) -> String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: List<String> = emptyList(), onLayoutChange: ((layout: List<String>) -> Unit)? = null, span: (T) -> MonarchDashboardGridSpan = { MonarchDashboardGridSpan.One }, columns: Int = DefaultColumns, editing: Boolean = false, state: LazyGridState = rememberLazyGridState(), labels: MonarchDashboardGridLabels = MonarchDashboardGridLabels(), itemContent: @Composable (item: T) -> Unit)

public class MonarchDashboardGridSpan { companion object { val One: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; val Two: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; val Full: MonarchDashboardGridSpan; fun columns(count: Int): MonarchDashboardGridSpan } }

public class MonarchDashboardGridLabels(label: String? = null, handle: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, earlier: String? = null, later: String? = null, moveEarlier: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, moveLater: ((label: String) -> String)? = null, pickedUp: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, moved: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, dropped: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null, cancelled: ((label: String, position: Int, total: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: items
options.description: The widgets in their default order.

options.name: key
options.description: A widget's stable, unique key, stored in layout.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: A widget's plain-text name, for the arrange bar, the button names and the announcements.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the grid. The grid scrolls itself; bound its height inside a scrolling parent.

options.name: layout
options.description: The order of keys saved for this person; empty for the default order. Unknown keys are skipped and new widgets appended.

options.name: onLayoutChange
options.description: Called with the whole new order after each finished move, for example to save it. Without it the grid cannot be rearranged.

options.name: span
options.description: The columns a widget spans, clamped to the columns available. Not applied in edit mode.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns from 1024dp of grid width, 1 to 4. From 640dp the grid has at most two, below it one.

options.name: editing
options.description: Shows an arrange bar on each widget with Move earlier and Move later, and makes the widgets draggable. Needs onLayoutChange.

options.name: state
options.description: The scroll state of the grid.

options.name: itemContent
options.description: Draws a widget, usually a MonarchWidget.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The widgets in rows with their spans; one column on phones and at font scale 1.5 and above.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each widget is a tile of MonarchSortableGrid with a drag handle and an arrange bar in the subtle background: the widget's name and Move earlier and Move later buttons, disabled at the ends.

states.name: dragged
states.description: The held widget follows the finger with the medium shadow and the accent border; the others slide out of its way.

appearance: Widgets are separated by 16dp. In edit mode each tile has the surface fill and subtle border of MonarchSortableGrid, and the arrange bar uses the subtle background role with small corners. Colors are theme roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web grid is a CSS grid with column spans in rem of grid width; Android uses a LazyVerticalGrid with fixed columns chosen from the grid's own width at the 640dp and 1024dp breakpoints, and one column from font scale 1.5. In edit mode the grid is a MonarchSortableGrid, which has no spans, so every widget takes one cell while editing. A long press drags a widget, as in Android launchers; the handle's actions and the Move earlier and Move later buttons replace the web's Space-and-arrow-keys pick-up. The web takes an uncontrolled defaultLayout and reports the move with its ids; Android hoists the layout as a list of keys and reports the whole new order, as iOS binds it. The web calls the handle "Move Team load"; Android keeps that name.
accessibility: The grid is a traversal group named "Dashboard".
In edit mode each widget has a drag handle named "Move Team load" with the move actions, a 48dp touch target, before the widget in both reading directions.
Move earlier and Move later are named with the widget ("Move Team load earlier"), have 48dp touch targets and are disabled at the ends.
Every move by a button or an action, and every pick up, drop and cancel of a drag, is announced through a polite live region: "Revenue moved to position 2 of 3."
At font scale 1.5 and above the grid has one column; widget names wrap at font scale 2.0.
Moves animate with the motion tokens and are immediate when animations are off.
edgeCases: A key in layout that is not an item is skipped; a repeated key counts once.
A span larger than the row takes the whole row; MonarchDashboardGridSpan.columns(0) is one column.
editing without onLayoutChange shows the viewing grid.
Keys must be unique; the same key twice breaks the lazy grid.
